props.title: Staying Inside the Picture

B36.capture_spec: C17: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex checker), lab-shaders/07-scale.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 13.3 s): zoom = 1 until 0.30 L, then 1 to 2 over 0.30-0.62 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state probes (fill-window): (0.25, 0.25) cream, (0.6, 0.05) and (0.9, 0.05) the same teal (constant along the row), (0.9, 0.9) cream (the corner pixel).
B36.visual_intent: Act title 'Staying Inside the Picture' (serif 40) top-left. Code card at left with the scale shader; at right a real Godot window where a teal-and-cream checker picture shrinks toward the top left as zoom goes from 1 to 2 and its edge rows and columns stretch into stripes across the rest of the square. A terracotta ring on the stripes with the readout 'edge pixels'.
B36.motion_claim: The picture shrinks and its edge pixels streak across the space it leaves.

show.event: uv = UV * zoom highlighted; the checker at full size
zoom grows; stripes stream out of the edges
the lookup keeps returning the last row and column; ring on the stripes

B36.why: The smear is an artifact on a real picture: the viewer should see the real thing before the mechanism.

B37.visual_intent: Two rows of edge pixels at the right edge of two pictures. Top row: a column of solid teal and cream edge pixels with horizontal stripes streaming outward to the right, labelled 'solid edge: stripes'. Bottom row: the same column drawn as dashed transparent cells, with nothing streaming outward, labelled 'transparent edge: nothing'. Small grey credit: 'Godot docs: a one pixel transparent border'.
B37.motion_claim: Stripes stream out of the solid edge; from the transparent edge nothing streams.

show.event: the two edge columns
stripes stream out of the solid edge
nothing streams from the transparent edge; the docs tip lands

B37.why: Edge pixels streaking outward, against transparent edge pixels streaking into nothing, is a mechanism drawing (and the docs' own tip).

B38.visual_intent: A plot with the horizontal axis from -1 to 2 and the vertical axis from 0 to 1: the curve of step(0, x), flat at 0 for x below 0 and flat at 1 from 0 on, with a terracotta dot travelling along it. Definition lines (GLOSSARY wording): 'mask: a number from 0 to 1 per pixel saying how much of something to show' and 'step(edge, x): 0 below the edge, 1 from the edge up'.
B38.motion_claim: The dot travels along the flat line at 0, jumps to 1 at the edge, and stays at 1.

show.event: axes and the step curve
the dot travels and jumps to 1 at zero (settled by 0.45)
the mask definition lands

B38.why: A plotted step with a dot jumping from 0 to 1 at the edge is what 'step' means.

B39.visual_intent: The same plot axes. The first step (turns on at 0) and the second step (turns off at 1) are drawn in two greys; they multiply into a terracotta box of height 1 between x = 0 and x = 1. Then a square picture-frame in the plane: ones inside, zeros outside, labelled 'both axes'.
B39.motion_claim: The two steps slide together and the product is a box between zero and one; the box then becomes a square in the plane.

show.event: the step that turns on at 0 and the step that turns off at 1
they multiply into a box (settled by 0.45)
the box becomes a square: both axes, multiply again

B39.why: Two steps multiplying into a one-only-between-zero-and-one gate is a function being built; a Manim plot does it with motion.

B40.capture_spec: C18: Lab sprite (--sprite-tex checker), lab-shaders/17-mask.gdshader. Keyframes (L about 10.2 s): zoom = 1 until 0.40 L, then 1 to 2 over 0.40-0.66 L, hold. Render L + 1 s, 30 fps, Forward+. End state probes (fill-window): (0.25, 0.25) cream, (0.75, 0.25) and (0.9, 0.9) stage colour (0.851, 0.835, 0.792), (0.495, 0.495) cream, (0.505, 0.505) stage.
B40.visual_intent: Code card at left with the mask shader (ten lines); at right the real Godot window with the same checker picture as the smear beat: as zoom goes from 1 to 2 it shrinks into the top-left quarter and the space it leaves stays empty, with no stripes. A terracotta ring on the empty space with the readout 'no smear'. A caption defines alpha (GLOSSARY wording): 'alpha: how visible a pixel is: 0 invisible, 1 solid'.
B40.motion_claim: The picture shrinks and the space it leaves stays clean.

show.event: COLOR.a *= inside.x * inside.y highlighted
inside: nothing changes
outside: alpha is zero; the picture shrinks cleanly
ring on the clean space: no smear

B40.why: The smear disappearing while the picture still shrinks is the proof the mask works.
